VISAGE / COMPLETE SYSTEM REPORT

Implementation, evaluation and delivery

November 23, 2026 · Six completed runs · Three pretrained models

Public source · Download release

Executive overview

VisAge is an implemented computer-vision web application that estimates one of three age groups from a selected face and compares three published pretrained vision backbones. The current system uses ConvNeXt V2 Nano, EfficientNetV2-S and Swin Transformer V2 Tiny, with Swin as the validation-selected default. The app supports uploads, camera capture, explicit face selection, face overlays, individual inference, Compare All, processing times and an offline evaluation dashboard.

The approved study contains six completed full-data runs: seeds 42 and 43 for each model. Every family serves its seed-42 best-validation checkpoint. Training remains stopped. The unfinished seed-44 run is preserved and excluded; nine supporting experiments are deferred. Independent pilot photo testing and further model improvements were explicitly excluded by the user. Physical webcam functionality was confirmed by the user; phone hardware testing is not required.

The selected Swin checkpoint achieved 92.70% age-group accuracy on the 3,492-image aligned validation split and 92.59% on the 3,493-image existing test benchmark. The shared redetection/alignment pipeline accepted 3,482 of 3,492 attempts (99.71% coverage). These measurements do not establish independent real-camera performance or actual-age verification.

1. Background and practical problem

Staff handling age-related checks must often decide when to request identification during restricted purchases or senior-discount requests. Facial appearance can provide an imperfect cue, but lighting, pose, image quality and individual variation can make visual judgments inconsistent. VisAge provides a comparative visual estimate and transparent model outputs to support a human review workflow. It does not determine legal age, recognize identity, approve a transaction or replace valid identification.

The project formulates the task as three-class image classification rather than numerical age regression. The groups are Under 18, ages 18-59 and 60+. A detector first finds candidate faces. A shared selection and alignment pipeline produces one canonical face image; each classifier then processes that same region. This formulation permits an interpretable comparison of two convolutional families and a hierarchical Transformer under common partitions and a recorded training budget.

The requested cosmetic refinements are implemented: the prototype badge and research branding were removed; the header lists the three models; the recommended model is first in displayed results; percentage headings read Model scores; the expandable score explanation and rejected-input reasons table were removed. Rejected inputs remain included in the aggregate evidence and all-attempted denominator. JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, BMP and single-page TIFF uploads are supported.

3. System architecture and data flow

The browser sends raw image bytes to a same-origin FastAPI service. A bounded admission queue serializes detector/model use and limits simultaneous retained uploads. The service decodes and orients the image, detects candidate faces, enforces face selection and quality conditions, aligns the selected face and runs one or all loaded classifiers. The response contains age-group labels, class scores, processing times and geometry metadata. Image objects are closed after each request; visitor images are not written to disk or added to training.

The evaluation dashboard reads saved, checksum-bound aggregate evidence for the loaded checkpoint hashes. It does not evaluate an uploaded person against an unknown true age. Classification, detector and shared-pipeline results have different datasets and denominators, which remain explicit in the API and interface.

5. Dataset provenance, audit and partition control

The retained study uses the aligned/cropped UTKFace mirror at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jangedoo/utkface-new, version 1. The archive contains 23,708 scanned files. The audit retained 23,285 samples and excluded 423; exact duplicate removal accounted for 364 images. It recorded 26 conflicting duplicate groups and 683 multi-image perceptual groups. Excluded paths were registered rather than silently deleted.

PartitionUnder 1818-5960+Total
Train2,92411,5331,84316,300
Validation6262,4713953,492
Test6272,4713953,493

The training partition contains 16,300 images, validation 3,492 and test 3,493. Duplicate/perceptual groups are kept together during assignment. The largest group has 12 images. The data is strongly imbalanced toward ages 18-59, motivating macro F1 and train-only class weighting. No age-group balancing sampler is added on top of the weighting.

UTKFace lacks reliable participant IDs; perceptual grouping is not proof of identity-independent partitions. Ages are dataset annotations, including automated estimates checked by annotators, not verified birth-record ages. The unavailable original archive had no author-published digest suitable for byte-for-byte mirror confirmation. The mirror archive checksum, extraction scope and local audit are recorded; this is provenance evidence, not a guarantee of original-photo rights. Dataset photos are excluded from public delivery.

6. The three model families and adapted heads

ConvNeXt V2 is a modern convolutional architecture associated with fully convolutional masked-autoencoder pretraining and global response normalization. The selected Nano checkpoint is convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in1k. EfficientNetV2 is a convolutional family designed around training and parameter efficiency; this study uses tf_efficientnetv2_s.in1k. Swin Transformer V2 uses hierarchical windowed attention; the selected Tiny checkpoint is swinv2_tiny_window8_256.ms_in1k. These backgrounds motivate architectural diversity; publisher benchmark results are not substituted for VisAge results. [1-3]

ModelFeaturesHead parametersTotal parameters
ConvNeXt V2 Nano6401,92314,984,723
EfficientNetV2-S1,2803,84320,181,331
Swin Transformer V2 Tiny7682,30727,580,461

Each model reconstructs the declared timm architecture, replaces the classification task with a linear three-logit head and strictly loads the complete selected checkpoint. The head has feature_dimension x 3 weights plus three biases. Softmax converts logits to three nonnegative scores whose total is approximately one. The maximum score selects the age-group class. The model registry pins architecture identifiers, input sizes, normalization and checkpoint provenance.

7. Shared preprocessing, detection and quality handling

Raw images pass byte-size and decoded-pixel limits, EXIF orientation and RGB normalization. The original JPEG/PNG/WebP decoder is preserved for research consistency. Additional still-image formats use a separate admission wrapper; a bounded JPEG preview is generated for browser display, while inference retains the original oriented RGB pixels. Multipage or animated inputs are rejected. This adds format support without training on preview recompression.

YuNet 2023mar supplies face boxes and five landmarks. The serving detector uses confidence 0.9, NMS 0.3, maximum detection side 1,280 and a cap of 10 faces. A missing face gives a typed error; multiple faces require explicit selection. The selected face must satisfy size, visibility, roll, alignment, brightness, blur and dynamic-range conditions. One five-point similarity alignment creates the shared 224-pixel canonical crop.

All classifiers use whole-face Pillow bicubic resizing to 224 and then 256 pixels, without an additional center crop. ConvNeXt and Swin use ImageNet mean/std; the selected TensorFlow EfficientNet checkpoint uses mean/std 0.5. This is a common adapted comparison recipe, not a claim to reproduce each publisher's original ImageNet evaluation setting. The selected face checksum is identical for every method in Compare All.

8. Training protocol and reproducibility

SettingRecorded value
Shared seeds42 and 43; exactly six completed full-data runs
Physical/effective batch32 / 32
Precision and layoutCUDA BF16 training; FP32 validation; channels-last tensors
OptimizerAdamW; backbone LR 0.0001; head LR 0.0005
RegularizationWeight decay 0.01; gradient clipping 5.0
StagesTwo head-only epochs, followed by backbone unfreezing and fixed cosine schedule
StoppingMinimum 8, maximum 24 epochs; patience 5; strict best validation macro F1
Class weightingNormalized inverse square root of training class counts; no additional balancing sampler
AugmentationIndependent horizontal flip 0.5; rotation -8 to +8 degrees; brightness/contrast/saturation 0.85-1.15; normalization after augmentation

Best-checkpoint selection uses the earliest highest validation macro F1. Later fine-tuning does not automatically replace an earlier better checkpoint. Training checkpoints preserve optimizer and RNG state for epoch-boundary continuation. All six completed selected artifacts, configs, histories, prediction CSVs and metadata were verified; complete checkpoint reloads reproduced every validation label and score, with maximum absolute difference 0.0 on the recorded reload check.

The original eighteen-job protocol remains preserved. A user-approved amendment, made after validation results had been observed, reduces completion scope to seeds 42 and 43. The unfinished Nano seed-44 run is retained but excluded; the other seed-44 jobs are unstarted. Three frozen-backbone and six data-efficiency jobs are deferred, with no invented results. Two seeds provide limited replication; means and sample standard deviations are descriptive, not evidence of statistical superiority.

9. Evaluation definitions and evidence scopes

MetricDefinition and interpretation
Accuracy (%)100 x correct age-group classifications / evaluated classification inputs
Precision / recallPer-class true positives divided by predicted positives / provided positives
F12 x precision x recall / (precision + recall), with the implementation's zero-denominator convention
Macro F1Unweighted mean of the three class F1 values; exposes imbalance more clearly than accuracy alone
Weighted F1Per-class F1 averaged by support
Confusion matrixRows: provided age group; columns: model prediction; counts and row-normalized rates
ROC / AUCOne age group versus the other two; complete scores generate ROC; macro AUC is the mean of class AUCs
Detection APArea under the detector precision-recall curve under the recorded IoU/ignore protocol; distinct from classification accuracy
CoverageAccepted images / every attempted pipeline input
All-attempted correct rateCorrect accepted predictions / every attempted pipeline input, including rejected photos in the denominator

The dashboard presents bounded display curves for responsiveness while retaining AUC values from complete saved scores. ROC AUC is independently checked using average ranks; confusion counts and other classification metrics are independently derived from checksum-bound prediction CSVs. Display scores for one person are uncalibrated softmax outputs, not verified probabilities of actual age. The UI intentionally labels them Model scores.

Nano seed 42 selects epoch 1 from head-only warm-up, although the run continued for eight epochs. Its subsequent fine-tuning did not exceed that score. Nano seed 43 selects fine-tuned epoch 16. Both EfficientNet and Swin serving checkpoints are fine-tuned. The report preserves this distinction rather than relabeling every selected checkpoint as fine-tuned.

Nano has a pronounced drop at the first unfrozen epoch in both seeds. Several runs develop a large gap between online training and validation macro F1. These are evidence of training instability and generalization limits worth reporting. The agreed best-validation rule preserves the strongest available checkpoint. No extra tuning was run to improve the appearance of these results.

15. Face-detector AP and provenance

The unchanged YuNet detector retains verified WIDER FACE validation evidence for 3,226 images and 39,112 valid ground-truth faces. AP at IoU 0.50 is 64.65%; AP at IoU 0.75 is 28.54%. Detector bytes, revision, annotations, provenance and saved prediction hashes were checked, together with twelve exact detector reload comparisons.

The AP protocol evaluates all valid boxes with the recorded ignore policy and all-point integration. It differs from the official WIDER easy/medium/hard leaderboard. Its sweep uses confidence floor 0.05, versus 0.9 in the application before face selection and quality checks. AP is detector evidence, not age-group accuracy or newly trained-detector performance. The dashboard includes precision-recall and FROC curves; compact runtime serialization preserves those curves without changing AP.

18. Browser implementation and score presentation

The interface uses a persistent workspace navigation, one photo source panel and result cards. A top status area names all three loaded models. The model selector, empty-state comparison and result cards place the recommended model first while API method IDs and output class order remain stable. The selected face overlay displays the estimate and clears whenever the photo, method or selection changes. Compare All uses one selected face for all methods.

Each model shows exactly three score rows: Under 18, 18-59 and 60+, with percentages, meters and a chosen-class marker. Raw numeric values remain in the API and CLI outputs. Very small positive scores display as less than 0.01% instead of rounding to exact zero; near-one scores can display as greater than 99.99%. There is no next-highest callout. The removed expandable explanation is absent, and percentage headings simply read Model scores. These cosmetic changes do not calibrate the model outputs or change the highest-score decision.

19. API contracts, admission and error handling

EndpointBehavior
GET /healthReadiness, loaded-model count and device
GET /v1/modelsModel IDs, names, selected default, seed/epoch, parameter count, artifact hashes and processing configuration
GET /v1/evaluationArtifact-bound aggregate classifier, detector, cost and shared-pipeline evidence
POST /v1/facesRaw supported image bytes; candidate boxes/landmarks and converted preview where needed
POST /v1/predictRaw image bytes; optional method and face index; one or three predictions, class scores, shared crop and timing

Queries use method=all or an exact active model ID; omitting method uses the serving-bundle default. Unknown legacy method IDs are rejected rather than silently aliased. Each prediction exposes method, class_id, age_group, class_scores, score_type, timing, manifest hash and device. class_scores contains three entries with class IDs 0, 1 and 2. The frontend validates labels, fixed order, finite range, approximate sum-to-one and agreement between the chosen class and the score maximum before rendering.

The local upload cap is 8 MiB and the decoded-image cap is 20 megapixels. The Vercel adapter advertises/enforces 4 MiB because the platform has a smaller request-body ceiling; the client displays that cap and rejects oversized input before transport. Errors distinguish empty/corrupt/unsupported/animated files, missing/multiple/small/unusable faces, queue saturation, timeouts and unavailable evidence. Internal exceptions do not leak stack traces to the browser. Request cancellation, stale-operation guards and URL revocation protect the image lifecycle.

20. Camera lifecycle, privacy and operational boundaries

The camera controller requests video only after an explicit action, supports preview, capture, retake and device switching, and shuts down tracks after capture or route departure. Browser camera access needs localhost or HTTPS. Simulated camera tests exercise permissions, late-acquired streams, switching, capture and track cleanup. The user independently confirmed that the physical webcam works correctly. Phone hardware acceptance was removed from scope by the user.

Visitor images are processed in memory, not saved, logged as image bytes or added to model training. The public repository and release do not include raw dataset photos, pilot participants, consent records, credentials or unfinished optimizer checkpoints. HTTP/browser security includes same-origin controls, no-store responses, bounded admission, explicit CORS origins when configured, a restrictive content-security policy and disabled microphone/geolocation permissions. The application does not implement identity verification, liveness/anti-spoofing, user accounts or transaction decisions.

23. Setup and operator guide

For a fresh CPU source checkout: install Python 3.12, create a virtual environment, install requirements.txt, run python scripts/download_runtime.py, then python scripts/serve_api.py --device cpu. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The complete delivery ZIP already contains runtime artifacts and therefore does not need the runtime download. The declared requirements still need to be installed. CUDA users should follow the recorded framework/environment instructions in the README.

To use the app, choose or capture one supported still photo. Select a face when multiple candidates are shown. Run the recommended model or Compare All. Inspect all three score rows and the age-group result, then apply the organization's identification policy. Replacing the photo or face clears results; use Retry for a lost connection and Reset to remove the preview. Evaluation tabs contain offline benchmark results, not uploaded-person accuracy.

The aligned-crop command is python scripts/predict.py FACE.png --method all. The raw-image command is python scripts/predict_image.py PHOTO.jpg --method all. The first assumes one already selected face; the second uses the shared detector/selection pipeline. Do not restart historical training controllers to run the app. Research reproduction additionally requires the frozen permitted dataset, full run artifacts and original protocol inputs.

24. Limitations, risks and responsible interpretation

The principal empirical limitation is domain transfer: aligned UTKFace crops and synthetic perturbations are not independent photos from the intended operational setting. Dataset labels are imperfect, and participant identity independence is unverified. Only two seeds were completed, and the approved scope amendment followed observation of validation results. The existing test benchmark was not previously untouched. These limitations constrain claims about generalization and statistical superiority.

There is no calibrated probability-of-age guarantee. Very high softmax scores can still be wrong, and ambiguous neighboring groups are especially relevant near age 18 and 60. The system has no liveness check or resistance to deliberate manipulation established by this study. The detector benchmark has a custom protocol and a different confidence operating point from serving. Overall correct rate must retain rejected attempts in its denominator. The selected ConvNeXt publisher weights have a noncommercial restriction; public code publication does not remove it or grant rights to dataset photos.

Operationally, PyTorch has a substantial dependency and cold-start footprint. GitHub Pages is a documentation host; the full inference API needs an appropriate backend. Vercel large-function eligibility, upload ceilings and account authorization must be checked in the actual deployment. Local latency measurements should not be advertised as cloud latency or multi-user capacity. The current package is verified in a fresh folder, with a separate clean-machine dependency installation still unclaimed.

Model experimentsIf reopened, investigate Nano unfreezing instability, more seeds, frozen-backbone controls and data-efficiency studies using training/validation onlyTraining stopped; nine supporting runs deferred

Recommendations are future options, not unfinished model-improvement actions in this delivery. The user requested that the models remain as they are and excluded pilot testing. Completing hosting authorization and checking the deployed API are deployment tasks; they do not require retraining or changing the selected validation rule.

26. Conclusions

VisAge now integrates three verified pretrained age-group classifiers into one consistent detection, selection, alignment and browser workflow. Six completed runs supply limited but explicit replication. The fixed two-seed validation rule selects Swin Transformer V2 Tiny, and the application preserves one seed-42 serving checkpoint per family. Swin has the strongest listed serving-checkpoint validation and existing-test results; EfficientNet is close in the family-mean comparison and faster in the recorded CPU timing. Nano is smaller and faster, with a materially weaker selected seed-42 result and a documented head-only best checkpoint.

The implementation is functionally verified through regression, real-artifact API/CLI checks, browser flows, CPU/CUDA consistency and a fresh, source-isolated archive extraction. All three class scores are visible, and the evaluation dashboard separates classifier accuracy, detector AP and pipeline coverage. The public repository, release assets and GitHub Pages documentation portal are established. Full Vercel-hosted inference remains dependent on team authorization and subsequent production checks. The resulting system is a review-support application with documented limits, not proof of an individual's chronological age or transaction eligibility.
